text:
maria: Quick check — I'm seeing traces for the background-batcher job where the root span exists but all child spans (db/http) are gone mid-run. Job logs show completion. Anyone seen this pattern? Trace link: https://observ.redwood/trace/abc123 :thinking_face:
ajay: Which runner is this (celery, k8s job, custom)? Also do you see exporter errors in the pod logs? :mag:
mar ia: it's a k8s CronJob -> Job -> pod (image: redwood/batcher:v2). No celery. Using python opentelemetry-sdk, auto-instrument requests + psycopg2. Trace id abc123 (link above). No obvious exporter errors in stdout but logs are sparse.
tess: Common suspects: 1) exporter batching + abrupt process exit (flush missed), 2) context lost across threads/processes, 3) sampling config (parent-based vs probabilistic) causing children to be dropped. Are you spawning subprocesses or forking?
jonathan: Also check envs in the job.yaml: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, OTEL_PROPAGATORS. If sampler is probabalistic <1.0 you'll randomly miss children if root wasn't sampled.
maria: Not forking or multiprocessing, we do a small ThreadPool for parallel DB calls. Here's the env snippet from the pod: `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceid`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otel-collector.namespace.svc:4317`, no explicit sampler arg.
ajay: Threading can still drop context if instrumentation/wrapping wasn't applied where threads are created. Also check exporter/bsp settings — if the process exits before the BatchSpanProcessor flushes, child spans may not be exported.
ajay: Quick commands to check logs and env: `kubectl logs -n batch job/batcher-job-xxxxx` and `kubectl exec -n batch pod/batcher-job-xxxxx -- env | egrep OTEL`
maria: Ah — we never call provider.shutdown() on graceful exit. Our exit handler just sys.exit(0). Example from our code: 
```python
# we create tracer provider but no shutdown
tracer_provider = TracerProvider()
# ... setup exporters/processors
# at end of job we just exit
```
tess: Try adding an explicit shutdown/flush on completion: `from opentelemetry import trace; trace.get_tracer_provider().shutdown()` or `tracer_provider.shutdown()` depending on your setup. Also for debugging set `OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` and `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY_MS=200` / `OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=1` to force more frequent flushes.
jonathan: For sampler checks you can temporarily set `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` for the job image or `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_always_on` to ensure everything gets sampled while you debug. Remember to revert to lower sampling in prod.
maria: Good call — i'll add shutdown and flip sampler to always_on for the next run. If it still happens I'll post trace id + timestamp.
ajay: Also verify that auto-instrumentation is imported before you create DB pools/clients. Order matters for a lot of Python libs (requests, psycopg2). Example: `from opentelemetry import auto_instrumentation` before `psycopg2.connect(...)`.
tess: Another quick thing: check the collector -> exporter path. If you're using OTLP over TLS and collector returns an error, exporter logs will show `Failed to export spans`. Search cluster logs for `Failed to export spans` or `exporter error`.
sre-bot: Runbook for lost spans: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/tracing/span-loss-checklist — steps: check exporter errors, enable debug logging, add shutdown, verify propagators, run always_on sampler for test.
maria: Thanks all — i'll push a small change (shutdown + sampler always_on + debug) and rerun. Will post the new trace id here when it's available. Appreciate the rapid help :pray:
ajay: :thumbsup: ping me once you have the trace id and i'll grep collector + exporter logs across the cluster for related errors.
sre-bot: Reminder: when posting trace id include pod start ts and job name so SRE can correlate with collector logs.
